newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish coalition deputies meet to settle row.
newsitem.headline: Polish coalition deputies meet to settle row.

text.p: Parliamentarians from Poland's Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) and the Polish Peasant Party (PSL) met on Tuesday to discuss the future of their government coalition and settle a rift over a planned cabinet reshuffle.

"The meeting was staged so we could agree together we trust each other...and that there is no need to include the opposition in the cabinet reconstruction," Jerzy Szmajdzinski, SLD leader, said before the meeting, expected to last well into the night. @

A crisis between ex-communist SLD and PSL erupted earlier this month when Peasant official Jacek Buchacz was removed by SLD Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz over alleged irregularities in his foreign trade ministry.
The sacking aggravated a dispute between the two parties over a forthcoming cabinet reshuffle, linked to a reorganisation of ministries under a reform aimed at streamlining cabinet decision-making.
Some PSL leaders have threatened their party could walk out of the coalition, paving the way for early general elections, otherwise not due until late next year. @
They say they may quit the coalition, which has survived several crices since its creation in late 1993, if PSL's demands of control over key portfolios are ignored by its bigger partner.
The rift concerns mainly appointments in three crucial economic ministries of economy, treasury and finance and the way the current cabinet would be transformed.
The SLD wants ministers to be replaced gradually beginning in October, when the cabinet reform is launched with the creation of a treasury ministry. @
The Peasant party says the whole current cabinet should be dismissed in a parliamentary vote and a new one promptly formed.
